vision_report.narrative_description: The observation sequence begins with a stable indoor biome featuring a young Mexican Mint in a black pot with a sensor (P2) and a Money Plant cutting in a white cup (Unmonitored). Both plants appeared healthy and stable from EARLIEST through T-3, with only minor variations in lighting and camera angle. A significant environmental anomaly occurred at T-2, where the scene became almost entirely dark, preventing any visual assessment. Lighting was restored at T-1, revealing the introduction of a white cylindrical object behind the Money Plant. At this point, the Money Plant showed subtle signs of reduced turgidity. The most dramatic changes are observed in the CURRENT image: the Money Plant and its propagation cup have been completely removed, representing a 'Systemic Loss'. Concurrently, the Mexican Mint plant is no longer visually discernible within its black pot, indicating either its removal or complete degradation, also classified as a 'Systemic Loss' of the visible specimen. The white cylindrical object has been removed, and a new red/orange spherical object has been introduced. The CURRENT image also suffers from severe underexposure, similar to T-2, making precise identification challenging. Overall, the biome has undergone significant compositional changes, primarily characterized by the loss of both monitored plant specimens and the introduction/removal of various desk surface items.
